title: Inverse Galois OQ-06→OQ-01: Eliminating three_dvd_gal_card
description: Progress on eliminating the last remaining axiom in InverseGaloisA5.lean: three_dvd_gal_card. Proves: q's root set in ℂ has cardinality 5, q is strictly monotone on ℝ, q has exactly one real root, complex conjugation is nontrivial, and 2 ∣ |Gal(q)|. Also proves q ≡ (X-5)(X-6)(cubic) mod 7 and the cubic has no roots in 𝔽₇. 16 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The inverse Galois problem asks which groups occur as Galois groups over ℚ. A₅ ≅ PSL(2,5) is realizable. A key tool is computing |Gal(q)| for the polynomial q = X⁵ − 5X⁴ + 10X³ − 10X² + 25X − 5.
overview.problemStatement: Make progress on proving 3 ∣ |Gal(q)| for q = X⁵ − 5X⁴ + ... − 5, the last step needed to force Gal(q) ≅ A₅.
overview.proofStrategy: Root analysis: |rootSet q ℂ| = 5 (degree 5). Derivative: q'(x) = 5(x-1)⁴ + 20 > 0 → q is strictly monotone → exactly 1 real root. Complex conjugation: nontrivial (2 | |Gal|). Mod 7 factorization: q ≡ (X-5)(X-6)(irreducible cubic) mod 7 → 3-cycles in Gal(q).
keyInsights: **Monotonicity approach**: q'(x) = 5(x-1)⁴ + 20 > 0 for all real x proves strict monotonicity, giving exactly one real root via IVT.
**Galois order divisibility**: complex conjugation (order 2) gives 2 | |Gal(q)|. Mod 7 factorization gives a 3-cycle.
**Mod 7 technique**: q factors as (linear)(linear)(cubic irreducible) mod 7, forcing a 3-cycle in Gal(q) via Frobenius, giving 3 | |Gal(q)|.
